testCase.name: [local] S13b A browser clock 2 days off, or a far time zone, stores the same admit date, hospital day and badge

descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · UAT 3.8; TFA-92579 AC 4 · “Every time-based rule (retention windows, carry-forward, the day roll to Follow-up, "today" on the timeline) uses the server clock.”. Mixed: stated part — hospital day / visit number and Follow-up badge are the same under a skewed browser clock or far time zone; our part — the stored admit date and the DOB-derived age on scanned rows (only the stated part makes a QA bug).

Bug B18 · S1 · known

Many dates and times follow the device clock instead of server time (UAT 3.8): 'NEW TODAY', admit date, vitals date, task done time, transcript date; with a phone two days slow a held drug is stamped two days back and the next cleanup deletes it

Tickets: TFA-92584 ready for qa (UAT 3.8); TFA-92597 ready for qa (R6); TFA-92579 AC 3/4 ready for qa (NEW TODAY); TFA-94745 ready for qa (draft restore) · counts as a QA bug: yes · found on: local

Note: Root cause known (Daniela asked for server time on 10-03); the deleted drug, missing badge and wrong draft restore are new symptoms. TC-16/S18 (UAT 3.8, one device set to the wrong date): a phone a day ahead files its bedside line in a row dated tomorrow on the shared record, and the next write from a correctly clocked device lists the lines before it twice (the transcript archive trusts the device date). Which calendar day a correct device should use when its local day and the server's UTC day differ is the open question Q9 (D10); TC-16/S25 passed otherwise. Review 2026-10-14 (TFA-92579/92584): a browser whose day is ahead writes the badge roll back to the server, and every device shows Follow-up, with the matching template and billing family (TC-01/S08, TC-20/S20a; TFA-92584 AC 8). The failing cell of TC-25/S24a is the card's NEW TODAY, which compares addedAt with the device's date (PatientCard.tsx:154-156). EFS/S28 (a)(b) restore drafts by the device date (TFA-94745); (c), an old draft put in today's box, is B13's. Review 2026-10-15 (TFA-94514): the analytics day is the device date too (pilotUsageEvents / pilotDailyRounding use localDay()): a phone 3 days ahead files its rows under its own day, and an encounter across the phone midnight is split over two days and never timed (OAT-06/S10). Re-test 2026-10-16 (TC-21/S26, 25acd727): a browser two days ahead writes the badge roll with its own future day (encTypeDay 2026-10-19) to the shared record, so the correct-clock browser shows Follow-up too. Re-test 2026-10-20 on 8b4be94a: changed: task done time and Important Points now use server time (TC-22/S23, TC-12/S23, TC-07/S28 stamp); still device time: Tomorrow's Pre-Round Summary edit (TC-17/S25), task screen header date (TC-07/S28), handoff title date (TC-08/S20), medicationsUpdatedAt (TC-19/S19), NEW TODAY (TC-01/S08), completeEncounter day (OAT-06/S10).

Other cases of the same bug (counted once): TC-01/S08, TC-10/S22, TC-12/S23, TC-19/S19, TC-22/S23, TC-25/S24a, EFS/S28, TC-16/S18, TC-06/S19, OAT-06/S10, TC-06/S23, TC-21/S22, TC-25/S24b, TC-19/S23, TC-21/S26, TC-17/S25, TC-07/S28, TC-08/S20

Approach · TC-02 Patient List Capture · S13b A browser clock 2 days off, or a far time zone, stores the same admit date, hospital day and badge

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U11 'Day 2' and the Follow-up rule follow the server clock, not the device clock. A device set to the wrong date shows the same state (3.8). (UAT 3.8)
  • U7 A scan never invents an MRN, room or name. A field the photo did not have is left blank and flagged. (UAT TC-02; TFA-92580 AC 6; TFA-92580 How it works 5; UAT 3.4) — gate: blocked: TFA-92580 rejected by qa
  • U9 Runs and passes in both contexts: the Hospital capture (camera icon) and the Nursing Home 'Scan Resident List' (3.3). (UAT 3.3; TFA-92580 How it works 1) — gate: blocked: TFA-92580 rejected by qa

Test design technique: Error guessing (error-guessing) — Go straight for the places most likely to break (failures, double clicks, two tabs, a wrong clock, injected instructions).

Given Local stack only, never dev or prod. Three fresh physicians. scan-probe runs the same mocked scans (the h-day1-clean rows, which have no admit-date or hospital-day column, and the n-day1-clean rows) in three runs: the real clock; …

When Each run scans and adds all rows in Hospital and in Nursing Home, then reads the list cards and the stored rows

Then All three runs store the same admit date (or leave it blank; Q13), show the same hospital day or visit number and the same Follow-up badge, and show the same age for a DOB-only resident

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): scan-probe compares the three runs' backend rows (rounding:list / snf:list: admitDate, dayNum, encType, age) and the card text. Any difference is a Fail. The day roll by device clock is known: TFA-92584. A device-dated admitDate (buildScannedPatient uses new Date()) is reported alongside it. A real phone set to the wrong date is the manual item in spec.manual

Where it ran: local probes (multi-device probes); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: browser agent (automated)

S13b is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-02.matrix.json; a letter suffix = one case split in several), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 0 rows.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 8b4be94a (10-20), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane probes.

Test method: PW · Playwright script (PW (page.clock and timezoneId, mocked scan)) — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on both; Source: probes.

UAT item: TC-02 Patient List Capture · Section: A1 · Home Screen & Dashboard · Scenario: TC-02/S13b

A browser clock 2 days off, or a far time zone, stores the same admit date, hospital day and badge

Tickets: TFA-92580 Patient List Capture (Scan Census OCR + manual add) (rejected by qa)

New local lane probes: status failed in probes/results.json → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue; part of it is a known gap)).

How it is tested (probes/plan.json, automatable: yes): scan-probe: three fresh physicians scan the same mocked rows (h-day1-clean, n-day1-clean) under the real clock, page.clock.setFixedTime(now + 2 d), and timezoneId Pacific/Kiritimati; compare rounding:list / snf:list fields (admitDate, dayNum, encType, age) and card text (random NH auto-MRN masked). [Review 2026-10-14] Time-zone leg pins the device clock to 11:00 UTC (before 10:00 UTC) so the UTC+14 date differs from UTC / Tokyo; a pinned-clock Tokyo control leg isolates the time zone from the pin. — Mocked rows at the socket + page.clock; real phone with wrong date stays manual (spec.manual).

Detail:

Re-checked after review 2026-10-14 (18:00 JST runs: fix-*.json). Real clock vs page.clock +2 d vs Pacific/Kiritimati with the device clock pinned to 11:00 UTC (UTC+14 date Oct 15 while UTC and Tokyo are Oct 14), plus a control with the same pinned clock in Tokyo. Hospital: real and control store admitDate 'Oct 14' with the 'NEW TODAY' badge; +2 d stores 'Oct 16' and Kiritimati 'Oct 15', both without the badge. NH rows identical in all runs (random auto-MRN masked). The control equals the real run, so the Kiritimati difference comes from the time zone, not the pinned clock. Side finding: with the device clock 2 days ahead an existing valid session is shown the sign-in screen at once (re-sign-in on that device works). Real phone with a wrong date stays manual (spec.manual).

Product issue: Known TFA-92584 (day logic by device clock) plus a device-dated admitDate: a physician whose phone date is 2 days ahead scans a census and every patient is stored as admitted 'Oct 16'; a physician whose phone is in a far-east time zone (UTC+14) where it is already tomorrow stores 'Oct 15'; in both cases without the 'New today' badge, while a colleague on a correct clock in Tokyo sees 'Oct 14' / New today. Breaks TC-02 S13b and ground rule 3.8.

Known gap (known): TFA-92584

Evidence: 5 attached.

Dev run: skipped: local-only — local-only — The given says local stack only, never dev or prod.. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
